required.check: Two-output Reformat: transform() returns 0 for accepted rows (written to $out.0) and 1 for rejected rows (written to $out.1); every row returns one of the two.
required.rationale: Returning OK/ALL or a single port for every row breaks the accepted/remediation split.

required.check: All four checks (REF, LIMIT, DATE, TERM) are evaluated for every row and each failure is recorded (e.g. appended to a list or separate flags), with no early return or else-if chain after the first failure; a row failing all four yields all four codes.
required.rationale: Stopping at the first failure turns REF;LIMIT;DATE;TERM into REF only.

required.check: Null, empty and whitespace-only invoice_limit_txt fail LIMIT without an exception (nvl/null check before trim and the pattern test; `str2decimal("")` throws).
required.rationale: An unguarded trim/str2decimal on null or empty text throws instead of reporting LIMIT.

required.check: The LIMIT grammar caps the integer part at 12 digits: 1234567890123 (13 digits) fails, 999999999999.99 passes (e.g. whole-string `~= "[0-9]{1,12}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"` or matches()).
required.rationale: A plain numeric test or str2decimal success accepts the 13-digit ceiling.

required.check: The LIMIT grammar is a whole-string match on the trimmed text that rejects a trailing decimal point ("1."), exponents ("1e2"), signs, currency symbols and grouping separators; it uses `~=` or matches(), not the substring operator `?=`, and not "str2decimal succeeds" (which accepts 1e2 / 1.).
required.rationale: Conversion-based validation accepts 1e2 and 1., which the spec rejects.

required.check: Impossible dates (2025-02-30) and shortened digits (2025-1-1) fail DATE via a strict check: either strict `isDate(d, pattern, ..., "UTC", true)`, a strict `str2date(...) : null` conditional-fail, or a regex shape check plus strict isDate (strict isDate alone is verified to reject both).
required.rationale: Lenient parsing rolls 2025-02-30 into March and accepts 2025-1-1.

required.check: Trailing characters ("2026-01-01x") fail DATE through an explicit whole-string shape check (regex such as `[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}( [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})?` with `~=`, or an equivalent length-plus-pattern test); strict isDate/str2date alone is not verified to reject trailing text.
required.rationale: Without a shape check, parsers that stop at the pattern end can accept 2026-01-01x.

required.check: Both yyyy-MM-dd and yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss are accepted, with the parse pattern chosen by the value's shape (or length); a supplied timestamp keeps its seconds in effective_dt (2026-02-28 12:34:56).
required.rationale: Parsing only the date-only pattern rejects valid timestamps or drops the time part.

required.check: effective_dt is parsed with the "UTC" time-zone argument (e.g. `str2date(d, p, "en.US", "UTC", true)`), so a date-only value becomes 00:00:00 UTC; date functions without a time zone use the host zone (CET).
required.rationale: Parsing in the host zone shifts date-only values by an hour in the UTC output field.

required.check: payment_term_txt is compared after trim and upperCase (null-safe, e.g. `upperCase(trim(nvl(x,"")))`): " net30 " passes, null/blank/"bad" fail TERM; business_code receives the normalized value while the source payment_term_txt field is left unchanged.
required.rationale: Comparing the raw text rejects " net30 "; normalizing in place corrupts the copied source field.

required.check: Accepted rows copy all input fields unchanged (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*;` or per-field), including vendor_ref_no with its outer spaces and the raw invoice/date/term texts, and set approved_amount from the validated trimmed limit, effective_dt and business_code.
required.rationale: Copying trimmed values or omitting the copy loses the original spelling the receiving teams reconcile on.

required.check: Rejected rows copy all input fields and set reject_reason to the failed codes in the order REF, LIMIT, DATE, TERM joined by ";" without spaces or a trailing separator (`join(";", list)` or equivalent concatenation); a whitespace-only vendor_ref_no (trim leaves "") yields REF.
required.rationale: Wrong order, spaces or a trailing ; breaks the remediation codes.

forbidden.check: A parse/conversion exception can escape where the spec requires a defined result: str2decimal/str2date is called on text that has not passed the grammar check (no guard). Valid guards: a prior regex shape check, strict isDate(...), or the conditional-fail form `str2date(...) : null` / `str2decimal(...) : null`.
forbidden.rationale: str2decimal("") and strict str2date on 2025-02-30 throw, failing the graph instead of routing the row to remediation.

forbidden.check: Returns SKIP or ALL (or writes both $out.0 and $out.1 and returns ALL) for some rows, so a row is dropped or reaches both destinations.
forbidden.rationale: Every source row must reach exactly one destination; SKIP drops it and ALL duplicates it.

T44.notes: Clause 4 trailing-character rejection stays an explicit shape-check item because strict isDate on trailing text is unverified. Old T44.2/T44.8 overlap removed: independence is .2, reason format is .12.

required.check: Two-output Reformat: transform() returns 0 for schedulable rows (written to $out.0) and 1 for correction rows (written to $out.1); every row returns one of the two.
required.rationale: Any other return scheme loses or duplicates enrollments.

required.check: Age, guardian, consent, visit and program defects are all collected for every row (no early return after the first defect); e.g. age 1e2 with null consent, 2026-02-30 and SENIOR yields AGE,CONSENT,VISIT,PROGRAM.
required.rationale: Stopping early reports AGE only for a multi-defect row.

required.check: age_txt is validated before conversion as trimmed whole-string 1–3 ASCII digits (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,3}"`); null, empty, signed, decimal and exponent forms ("1e2") fail AGE and str2integer is not called for them.
required.rationale: Converting first throws on 1e2 or empty text.

required.check: A grammatically valid age is accepted only between 0 and 120 inclusive: 121 fails AGE, 0 is a valid (minor) age.
required.rationale: Off-by-one bounds misclassify 0 or 121.

required.check: For a valid age under 18, a null or whitespace-only guardian_id (trimmed, null-safe) produces GUARDIAN; age 0 with null guardian yields GUARDIAN.
required.rationale: Testing only null misses " "; testing only blank throws or misses null.

required.check: GUARDIAN is never produced when the age is invalid (1e2, empty, 121) or the age is 18 or older (18 with null guardian is accepted).
required.rationale: Applying the guardian rule to an unparsed/default age 0 adds a fictitious GUARDIAN defect.

required.check: consent_txt passes only when `upperCase(trim(...))` equals "Y" ("y" and " Y " pass); N, null, blank and other text produce CONSENT, independently of age or guardian.
required.rationale: Comparing raw text rejects " Y "; inferring consent from a guardian accepts N.

required.check: visit_day_txt must have the exact whole-string yyyy-MM-dd shape: time-bearing "2026-04-01 00:00:00" and shortened "2026-4-1" fail VISIT (regex shape check, or strict isDate for short digits; trailing time text needs the explicit shape check). Trimming visit_day_txt first or not is both acceptable.
required.rationale: A lenient or prefix parse accepts the time-bearing string the spec rejects.

required.check: A well-shaped visit day must be a real calendar date (strict check: 2026-02-30 fails) and lie between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-30 inclusive (04-30 passes, 05-01 fails); the range test may compare typed dates or the validated yyyy-MM-dd strings lexicographically.
required.rationale: Exclusive bounds drop 04-30; lenient parsing accepts 02-30.

required.check: appointment_day is produced with the "UTC" time-zone argument (e.g. `str2date(d, "yyyy-MM-dd", "en.US", "UTC", true)`), giving midnight UTC; functions without a zone use the host zone (CET).
required.rationale: Host-zone parsing writes 2026-03-31 23:00 UTC for 2026-04-01.

required.check: program_txt is trimmed and upper-cased; WELL passes for any age (an invalid age adds no PROGRAM defect), SENIOR passes only with a valid age >= 65 (64 fails, 65 passes, invalid age fails), any other code fails PROGRAM.
required.rationale: Using the default age 0 or skipping the age-validity condition misjudges SENIOR.

required.check: Correction rows copy all source fields unchanged and set correction_codes to the defects in the order AGE, GUARDIAN, CONSENT, VISIT, PROGRAM joined by "," (no spaces, no trailing comma); accepted rows copy the source fields and add patient_age, appointment_day and normalized_program.
required.rationale: Wrong order or separators break the correction contract.

forbidden.check: A parse/conversion exception can escape where the spec requires a defined result: str2integer on age_txt or str2date on visit_day_txt is called on text that has not passed the grammar check (no guard). Valid guards: a prior regex shape check, strict isDate(...), or the conditional-fail form `str2date(...) : null` / `str2decimal(...) : null`.
forbidden.rationale: str2integer("1e2") and strict str2date("2026-02-30") throw instead of producing AGE/VISIT.

forbidden.check: Returns SKIP or ALL (or writes both $out.0 and $out.1 and returns ALL) for some rows, so a row is dropped or reaches both destinations.
forbidden.rationale: Every source row must reach exactly one destination; SKIP drops it and ALL duplicates it.

T45.notes: Clause 5 does not say whether visit_day_txt is trimmed (reference does not trim); both are accepted. Lexicographic range comparison on a validated yyyy-MM-dd string is accepted.

required.check: Two-output Reformat: transform() returns 0 for valid manifests (written to $out.0) and 1 for invalid ones (written to $out.1); every row returns one of the two.
required.rationale: Any other return scheme loses or duplicates manifests.

required.check: movement_txt is trimmed and upper-cased; only SHIP and REVERSE are recognized, null/blank/other fail MOVEMENT, and an unrecognized movement does not suppress the QTY, VALUE and DISPATCH checks ("?" with null quantity yields MOVEMENT|QTY|VALUE|DISPATCH).
required.rationale: Returning early on an unknown movement hides the other defects.

required.check: quantity_txt grammar is a whole-string match on the trimmed text of an optional minus and 1–6 digits (e.g. `~= "-?[0-9]{1,6}"`): "+2", null and blank fail QTY, and str2integer is called only after the grammar passes.
required.rationale: Converting before the grammar check accepts +2 or throws on null.

required.check: After the grammar passes, SHIP requires a positive quantity and REVERSE a negative one (REVERSE 2 fails QTY); an unrecognized movement applies no sign rule.
required.rationale: Ignoring the movement-dependent sign accepts a positive reversal.

required.check: A zero quantity always fails QTY, including "-0" for REVERSE and 0 for SHIP (test the converted value, not the text).
required.rationale: A text test for a leading minus accepts -0 as a negative reversal.

required.check: unit_value_txt is validated as a whole-string match of 1–8 integer digits with optional 1–2 fraction digits, no sign (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,8}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`): "1e2" and empty fail VALUE, 99999999.99 passes, and 0 is valid (not treated as missing).
required.rationale: Conversion-based checks accept 1e2; a zero test treats 0 as missing.

required.check: For REVERSE, ORIGINAL is reported when trimmed original_manifest is null/blank or equals trimmed manifest_id (self-reference M0/M0 fails).
required.rationale: Checking only null misses the self-reference reversal.

required.check: For SHIP or an unrecognized movement, original_manifest is not checked at all (SHIP with "x" and "?" with "x" get no ORIGINAL).
required.rationale: Applying the reversal rule to every row adds spurious ORIGINAL defects.

required.check: dispatch_txt must be exactly 8 digits by an explicit whole-string shape check (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{8}"` or length 8 plus digits): "202611" and "20260101x" fail DISPATCH; strict date parsing alone is not verified to reject trailing text. Trimming first or not is both acceptable.
required.rationale: Without a shape check a suffix after a valid day may be accepted.

required.check: A well-shaped dispatch_txt must be a real calendar day (strict isDate/str2date: 20260230 fails, 20240229 passes) and dispatch_day is parsed with the "UTC" time-zone argument so it is midnight UTC.
required.rationale: Lenient parsing accepts 20260230; host-zone parsing shifts the day by an hour.

required.check: declared_value is the signed quantity times the unit value as a decimal (e.g. `qty * str2decimal(v)`), negative for REVERSE (-2 × 1.25 = -2.50), and signed_quantity is the converted signed integer; raw source fields are copied unchanged.
required.rationale: Using abs() or the unsigned text loses the reversal sign.

required.check: Rejected rows copy all fields and set defect_list to the defects in the order MOVEMENT, QTY, VALUE, ORIGINAL, DISPATCH joined by "|" with no trailing separator.
required.rationale: Wrong order or separator breaks the broker evidence.

forbidden.check: A parse/conversion exception can escape where the spec requires a defined result: str2integer/str2decimal/str2date is called on text that has not passed the grammar check (no guard). Valid guards: a prior regex shape check, strict isDate(...), or the conditional-fail form `str2date(...) : null` / `str2decimal(...) : null`.
forbidden.rationale: str2integer("+2"), str2decimal("1e2") or strict str2date("20260230") throw instead of producing a defect.

forbidden.check: declared_value is computed through number (double) arithmetic, e.g. decimal2double, a `number` variable or a floating intermediate that is then rounded.
forbidden.rationale: 99999899990000.01 is not representable exactly as a double; the spec requires exact decimal arithmetic.

forbidden.check: Returns SKIP or ALL (or writes both $out.0 and $out.1 and returns ALL) for some rows, so a row is dropped or reaches both destinations.
forbidden.rationale: Every source row must reach exactly one destination; SKIP drops it and ALL duplicates it.

T46.notes: Clause 6 does not say whether dispatch_txt is trimmed (reference does not trim); both accepted.

required.check: Single-output Reformat: transform() writes $out.0 and returns OK (or 0 / ALL) for every policy; no row is skipped.
required.rationale: Returning SKIP for any row loses a migrated policy.

required.check: policy_number = trim(legacy_policy_no); a trimmed empty identifier becomes UNASSIGNED.
required.rationale: Copying the raw identifier keeps outer spaces; missing the default leaves an empty key.

required.check: billing_mode is trimmed and upper-cased null-safely: M → MONTHLY, A → ANNUAL, null/blank/unknown → MANUAL (" M " maps to MONTHLY).
required.rationale: Comparing the raw code maps " M " to MANUAL.

required.check: UNKNOWN_MODE is added only for a nonblank unrecognized billing code ("bad", "?"), not for null or blank billing_mode.
required.rationale: Treating null as unknown adds a spurious warning.

required.check: manual_override null and empty are distinguished: null means no override (source mode kept), while a non-null override that trims to empty forces MANUAL (" M " with override "" → MANUAL). `isBlank(override)` / `trim(nvl(override,"")) == ""` as the 'no override' test is wrong here.
required.rationale: Collapsing "" into null keeps MONTHLY where the spec demands MANUAL.

required.check: A trimmed, upper-cased override of M or A replaces the computed mode with MONTHLY or ANNUAL (unknown "?" source with override "m" → MONTHLY).
required.rationale: Ignoring a lowercase override keeps MANUAL.

required.check: Any other nonblank override adds BAD_OVERRIDE and leaves the source-computed mode unchanged (billing m, override "?" → MONTHLY with BAD_OVERRIDE).
required.rationale: Resetting the mode to MANUAL on a bad override discards the valid source mode.

required.check: suspended true forces mode_cd HOLD after both codes are applied; false or null is not suspended, tested null-safely (e.g. `nvl($in.0.suspended, false)` or `$in.0.suspended == true`).
required.rationale: Applying HOLD before the override lets the override win; an unguarded null boolean test can fail.

required.check: Warnings survive suspension: migration_warning lists UNKNOWN_MODE before BAD_OVERRIDE joined by ";" even when mode_cd is HOLD, and is the empty string (not null) when there are none.
required.rationale: Clearing warnings on HOLD or emitting null for none violates clauses 4 and 8.

required.check: display_nm is trimmed and becomes "Unnamed" when null or blank.
required.rationale: Missing the null/blank default leaves null or " " names.

required.check: email_txt stays null when null; otherwise it is trimmed and lower-cased, so empty stays empty (" B@C " → "b@c"); it is never defaulted because the name was defaulted.
required.rationale: lowerCase(trim(nvl(email,""))) turns null into "".

required.check: credit_balance, retired_at and all other retained fields are copied unchanged by name (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*;` or per-field), keeping negative/null balances and the time part of retired_at (1970-01-01 12:00:00).
required.rationale: Rounding, truncating or defaulting these values alters migrated data.

forbidden.check: Copies fields by position between the different input and output schemas (copyByPosition or index-based field access), shifting values after the removed columns.
forbidden.rationale: The output drops columns, so positional copy misaligns every following field.

forbidden.check: Writes to output fields that do not exist in PolicyDestination (e.g. $out.0.legacy_policy_no, $out.0.billing_mode, $out.0.old_policy_memo).
forbidden.rationale: Those fields were removed from the output schema, so the CTL does not compile.

T47.notes: Key discriminator is .5 (null vs empty override). Single-output contract: OK/0/ALL all accepted.

required.check: Normalizer contract: count() returns the number of child rows for the current property (retained owners, or 1 for the placeholder) and transform(integer idx) builds child idx on $out.0 and returns OK.
required.rationale: A Rollup/Reformat-style single transform() does not normalize one parent into several rows.

required.check: parcel_number = trim(old_parcel_id), with UNKNOWN_PARCEL when the trimmed value is empty.
required.rationale: Copying the raw id keeps " P1 "; missing the default leaves an empty parcel.

required.check: owners_txt is split on ";" (null handled with nvl or an explicit check), each segment trimmed, and empty segments from leading, trailing or repeated delimiters discarded; other punctuation ("X.Y") stays part of the name.
required.rationale: Keeping empty segments emits blank owners and inflates the count.

required.check: Duplicates within one property are removed case-insensitively after trimming (e.g. upperCase/lowerCase key in a map), keeping the first spelling and first-appearance order (" Ann ;bob;ANN; ;Bob;" → Ann, bob).
required.rationale: Case-sensitive dedup keeps ANN and Bob; keeping the last spelling changes names.

required.check: A property with no usable owner (null, empty, whitespace or delimiter-only " ; ; ") emits exactly one row with owner_name UNKNOWN_OWNER, owner_missing true, owner_ordinal 1 and owner_total 1; real owner rows have owner_missing false.
required.rationale: Missing the placeholder loses the parcel; flag errors misreport ownership.

required.check: owner_ordinal is idx + 1 in retained order and owner_total is the retained count after blank removal and dedup (2 for the first property, not 5 or 6).
required.rationale: Counting separators gives the wrong total.

required.check: tenure_txt is trimmed and upper-cased null-safely: F → FREEHOLD, L → LEASEHOLD ("f" and "l" too), null/empty/unknown → UNVERIFIED, written on every child row.
required.rationale: Comparing raw codes maps "f" to UNVERIFIED.

required.check: Tenure (and parcel/missing values) is derived from the current property each time, so a property with "?" after a LEASEHOLD property gets UNVERIFIED rather than a borrowed value.
required.rationale: Keeping the tenure variable from the previous parent when the current code is missing leaks LEASEHOLD.

required.check: The owner list and dedup set are reset for every property (either clear()/reassign in count(), clear in clean(), or fresh declarations per parent), so "Bob" in a later P1 row is emitted again.
required.rationale: Without a reset the second P1's Bob is deduplicated against the first property and lost.

required.check: Each child carries the parent's other fields unchanged (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*;` in transform, or a copy of the parent record saved in count()), including null/negative assessed_value, registered_at with time and street_label null vs empty.
required.rationale: Missing the copy leaves the property attributes empty on owner rows.

forbidden.check: transform(idx) indexes the raw split result (e.g. `parts[idx]`) while count() returns the retained count, or count() returns a different number than the list transform() reads.
forbidden.rationale: Blank or duplicate segments then shift names or raise an index-out-of-bounds error.

forbidden.check: count() returns 0 for a property with null, blank or delimiter-only ownership.
forbidden.rationale: A Normalizer emits nothing when count() is 0, so the parcel disappears.

T48.notes: Old T48.8 'do not expose ownership text' dropped (output has no owners_txt field; it could never fail).

required.check: Single-output Reformat: transform() writes $out.0 and returns OK (or 0 / ALL) for every entry; the carried balance, ordinal and previous key live in global variables that persist between calls.
required.rationale: Local-only state cannot carry balances across records.

required.check: account_key = trim(old_account), and the account change test compares trimmed keys (" A " continues account A as entry 2).
required.rationale: Comparing raw keys starts a new account at " A ".

required.check: The first record is handled so that a blank key is a legitimate account: either an explicit first-record flag/counter, or a plain `k != previous` comparison relying on the declared defaults (previous "", balance 0, ordinal 0). A sentinel such as `previous == ""` / isBlank(previous) fails: the three leading blank-key rows must be numbered 1, 2, 3 with balance 2.00, 2.00, 0.00.
required.rationale: An empty-string sentinel resets the blank account on every row.

required.check: When the trimmed key differs from the previous entry, balance and ordinal are reset to zero before the current entry is applied (B after A starts at 0.00, entry 1).
required.rationale: Resetting after applying the entry or not at all carries A's balance into B.

required.check: entry_kind is trimmed and upper-cased null-safely; OPEN sets the balance to opening_balance, with null meaning zero (`nvl(opening_balance, 0D)`), ignores movement_amount, and a second OPEN replaces the earlier balance.
required.rationale: Adding instead of replacing, or a null opening, corrupts the balance.

required.check: MOVE with non-null movement_amount adds it to the balance, including zero and negative amounts, with status OK.
required.rationale: Skipping zero/negative amounts loses movements.

required.check: MOVE with null movement_amount leaves the balance unchanged and reports MISSING_AMOUNT, with no arithmetic on the null value.
required.rationale: balance + null throws or nulls the non-nullable balance.

required.check: CLOSE sets the balance to zero regardless of the numeric fields and reports CLOSED; the row is still emitted.
required.rationale: Keeping the balance or skipping the row breaks clause 5.

required.check: Unknown, blank or null entry_kind reports UNKNOWN_KIND and leaves the balance unchanged ("??" in A keeps 7.50).
required.rationale: Treating unknown kinds as zero resets loses the carried balance.

required.check: migration_status is decided fresh for every entry (e.g. a local status initialized to OK each call), so OK follows a MISSING_AMOUNT or UNKNOWN_KIND entry.
required.rationale: A global status carries a previous defect forward.

required.check: migrated_balance is the balance after the current entry, account_entry_no is the per-account ordinal starting at 1, and all original fields are copied unchanged (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*;` or per-field), including raw entry_kind.
required.rationale: Writing the pre-entry balance or a global row number misreports history.

forbidden.check: Resets account_entry_no (or treats the row as a new account) on CLOSE or OPEN instead of only on a key change.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 5 says a later MOVE continues the same account; only a key change starts one.

forbidden.check: Declares the carried balance or ordinal as a local variable inside transform() (reset on every record).
forbidden.rationale: Balances and ordinals then never carry from one entry to the next.

T49.notes: First-record sentinel: plain `k != previous` with declared defaults is functionally correct here and accepted; `previous == null` is harmless dead code (never true) and not penalised; only an empty-string sentinel breaks the blank account.

required.check: Single-output Reformat: transform() writes $out.0 and returns OK (or 0 / ALL) for every shipment, including misses.
required.rationale: Skipping misses loses shipments.

required.check: carrier_cd and service_cd are trimmed and upper-cased null-safely only for the lookup keys; the raw values are copied unchanged to the output (" a " stays " a ").
required.rationale: Writing the normalized keys over the source fields changes raw spelling.

required.check: No ServiceRules query is made when either normalized key is empty (null or blank) or pickup_day is null; such rows get the missing-reference result.
required.rationale: Querying with blank keys or comparing a null pickup_day misclassifies or throws.

required.check: The queries run in order exact (carrier, service) → (carrier, "*") → ("*", "*") via `lookup(ServiceRules).get(a, b)`, and reference_level is EXACT, CARRIER or NETWORK by the stage that supplied the selected record, not by rule_label.
required.rationale: Wrong order or label-based levels misreport the commitment source.

required.check: An exact (or carrier) record that exists but is ineligible does not end the search: an expired exact hit (pickup one second after valid_to) falls back to CARRIER, a negative sla_days exact record falls back to CARRIER.
required.rationale: Stopping at the first non-null record uses an expired commitment.

required.check: Eligibility bounds are inclusive and compared on the full typed timestamps: pickup_day exactly at valid_from or exactly at valid_to is eligible, one second after valid_to is not.
required.rationale: Exclusive comparisons reject boundary pickups; day truncation accepts the late one.

required.check: A null valid_to means no upper limit (record eligible from valid_from on).
required.rationale: Comparing against null valid_to rejects open-ended rules.

required.check: sla_days must be null or >= 0 for eligibility; a selected record with null sla_days gives sla_days 5 with reference_miss false.
required.rationale: Treating a null sla as a miss sets reference_miss true wrongly.

required.check: A selected sla_days of 0 is used unchanged (not replaced by 5).
required.rationale: A truthiness/positive test turns the zero-day commitment into 5.

required.check: When no stage yields an eligible record: sla_days 5, reference_miss true, reference_level NONE.
required.rationale: Missing defaults leave fields unset or stale.

required.check: On a miss, reference_key is the normalized carrier, ":", and the normalized service, with null or blank parts as empty strings (":" for both empty, ":EXP" for null carrier). Setting reference_key the same way on hits is also acceptable.
required.rationale: Using raw keys or the string "null" breaks the diagnostic key.

required.check: Every row starts from its own defaults (e.g. assign sla 5 / miss true / NONE first, or assign all four computed fields on every path) and lookup results are held in local variables, so a miss after a hit does not inherit the hit's values.
required.rationale: Global or unassigned outputs leak the previous shipment's commitment.

forbidden.check: Reads fields of a lookup result without first checking that it is not null (e.g. `r.valid_from` after `get` returned null), with none of `r == null`, `isnull(r)` or `count(...) > 0` as a guard.
forbidden.rationale: A missing exact key (carrier B) then throws instead of falling back.

forbidden.check: Truncates pickup_day or valid_from/valid_to to the day (trunc, date2str, a day-based dateDiff) before comparing.
forbidden.rationale: A pickup one second after valid_to becomes eligible, keeping an expired exact rule.

T50.notes: Spec gap: clause 7 defines reference_key only for misses; the reference sets it on every row (A:EXP on hits). The item accepts both. Owner may want to state the hit value in the prompt.

required.check: Single-output Reformat: transform() writes $out.0 and returns OK (or 0 / ALL) for every claim, including misses.
required.rationale: Skipping misses loses claims.

required.check: provider_id and region_id are trimmed and upper-cased null-safely for the query only (raw values copied); a null/blank key or null loss_at makes no query and gives the missing-tariff result.
required.rationale: Raw keys miss " p "; querying with a null loss_at compares against null.

required.check: All candidates for the key are read: `get(a, b)` followed by `next()` until null (while loop), or a loop bounded by `count(a, b)` with get then next(). The graph lookup is configured with keyDuplicates=true, so a single get() sees only the first candidate.
required.rationale: Reading only get() ignores competing tariffs and picks by table order.

required.check: A candidate is eligible only when effective_from <= loss_at and (effective_to is null or loss_at <= effective_to), compared on full timestamps (a loss one second after effective_to is ineligible; a loss before every effective_from finds nothing).
required.rationale: Open-ended or boundary errors select expired or future tariffs.

required.check: payout_percent must be non-null and between 0 and 100 inclusive: 101 and null are ineligible, and a 0 percentage is a valid winner.
required.rationale: Missing the range check lets a 101% tariff win; treating 0 as missing loses the ZERO tariff.

required.check: Among eligible candidates the latest effective_from wins, regardless of lookup order.
required.rationale: Taking the first or last returned candidate depends on table order.

required.check: Ties on effective_from are broken by the lowest admin_fee (LOW with fee 3.00 loses to fee 2.00).
required.rationale: Ignoring the fee picks the wrong tariff among same-day candidates.

required.check: Remaining ties are broken by the lexicographically smallest tariff_id (A beats B at equal date and fee).
required.rationale: Without the id tie-break the winner depends on lookup order.

required.check: payout is computed in decimal arithmetic as claim_amount * payout_percent / 100 with decimal operands (e.g. `100D`), never via number/double.
required.rationale: Double arithmetic can turn 0.005 into 0.00499… and round down.

required.check: payout is rounded explicitly with `round(x, 2)` on the decimal value (rounds half away from zero: 0.02 × 25% = 0.005 → 0.01).
required.rationale: Relying on implicit scale or truncating gives 0.00 instead of 0.01.

required.check: A null or negative claim_amount gives payout 0 while the winner is still reported (selected_tariff set, tariff_missing false); a zero amount gives payout 0 and is not a miss.
required.rationale: Treating a null amount as a miss or computing with it misreports the tariff.

required.check: With no eligible candidate (including a key hit whose candidates are all ineligible) selected_tariff is "", tariff_missing true and payout 0.
required.rationale: Missing defaults leave null or stale outputs.

forbidden.check: Keeps the winning record or found flag in global variables that are not reset at the start of each claim.
forbidden.rationale: A miss after a zero-percent hit then reuses the previous tariff.

forbidden.check: Subtracts or otherwise applies admin_fee to the payout.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 4 says the fee is only a tie-break and is never deducted.

forbidden.check: Reads fields of the record returned by get()/next() before checking it for null (e.g. a do-while that reads r.effective_from on a miss).
forbidden.rationale: A queryable key with no tariff records then throws instead of producing the miss result.

T51.notes: Spec says 'rounded half-up'; CTL2 round(decimal,2) rounds half away from zero, identical for the non-negative payouts here, so explicit round(...,2) is required. keyDuplicates=true is a graph setting stated in .3.

required.check: Two-output Reformat: transform() returns 0 for calibrated samples (written to $out.0) and 1 for corrections (written to $out.1); every row returns one of the two.
required.rationale: Any other return scheme loses or duplicates samples.

required.check: facility_txt is trimmed and upper-cased null-safely; null or blank adds FACILITY; the raw value is copied unchanged (" f1 " stays).
required.rationale: Writing the normalized key over the source changes the sample record.

required.check: The assay grammar is a whole-string match on the trimmed, upper-cased value of a letter followed by 1–5 letters/digits (e.g. `~= "[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,5}"`): "ab" passes as AB, "?" fails ASSAY, independently of the reference tables.
required.rationale: Testing only table presence or skipping the grammar misreports ASSAY.

required.check: result_txt grammar is a whole-string match on the trimmed text of an optional minus, 1–6 integer digits and optional 1–3 fraction digits (e.g. `~= "-?[0-9]{1,6}(\\.[0-9]{1,3})?"`): "1e2", empty and "1234567" fail VALUE; 0 and -1.002 pass.
required.rationale: str2decimal-based checks accept 1e2 and 7-digit values.

required.check: FACILITY, ASSAY and VALUE defects are all collected and joined in that order with ";" (null facility, "?", "1e2" → FACILITY;ASSAY;VALUE; blank facility and empty result → FACILITY;VALUE).
required.rationale: Stopping at the first syntax defect or misordering breaks the correction reason.

required.check: Neither lookup table is queried when any syntax defect exists.
required.rationale: Clause 5 forbids queries for syntactically invalid input.

required.check: A facility record with enabled false yields the single reason BLOCKED and does not fall back to the assay default (F2 with a valid AB default is still BLOCKED).
required.rationale: Falling back on a disabled facility rescues a blocked measurement.

required.check: The facility factor is used only when enabled is true and factor is non-null, > 0 and <= 1000000; null enabled, null factor or a factor over 1000000 falls back to the assay default (F3, F4, F5 → DEFAULT).
required.rationale: Treating null enabled as disabled blocks a valid fallback; skipping the bound uses 1000001.

required.check: A missing facility record also falls back to the assay default (UNKNOWN facility → DEFAULT 2.50).
required.rationale: Rejecting on a missing facility record skips the general standard.

required.check: The default factor is usable only when non-null, > 0 and <= 1000000; zero, null, over-limit or a missing default record gives the single reason NO_FACTOR.
required.rationale: Accepting a zero or over-limit default calibrates with an invalid factor.

required.check: calibrated_result = round(str2decimal(trimmed result) * factor, 2) in decimal arithmetic, with factor_used and factor_source FACILITY or DEFAULT; `round(x, 2)` rounds half away from zero (-1.002 × 2.50 = -2.505 → -2.51) and is accepted for 'half-up'.
required.rationale: Unrounded or double arithmetic misstates the calibrated value.

forbidden.check: A parse/conversion exception can escape where the spec requires a defined result: str2decimal on result_txt (including while building a reject row) is called on text that has not passed the grammar check (no guard). Valid guards: a prior regex shape check, strict isDate(...), or the conditional-fail form `str2date(...) : null` / `str2decimal(...) : null`.
forbidden.rationale: str2decimal("1e2") or str2decimal("") throws instead of producing VALUE.

forbidden.check: Reads fields of a lookup result before checking it for null (e.g. `f.enabled` when FacilityFactors.get returned null), with no `== null`, isnull() or count() guard.
forbidden.rationale: A missing facility record (UNKNOWN) then throws instead of falling back to the default.

forbidden.check: Keeps the selected factor or factor_source in global variables that are not reset for each sample.
forbidden.rationale: A failed lookup after a success then reuses the earlier factor (clause 9).

T52.notes: Spec gap: 'rounded half-up' is ambiguous for negatives; CTL2 round() rounds half away from zero (reference -2.505 → -2.51). Item .11 accepts round(x,2); owner may reword clause 8 to 'half away from zero'.

required.check: DataIntersection contract: transform() handles matched pairs only ($in.0 previous, $in.1 incoming), writes the result to `$out.0` and returns an emitting value (OK, 0, 1 or ALL). Verified by live runs: the matched record written to CTL `$out.0` is emitted on physical port 1, and writing `$out.1` fails at graph init (ctl2-basics §8.9 still says `$out.1` and is outdated). One-sided records are passed through by the component with no CTL code; unused transformLeftOnly/transformRightOnly declarations are harmless.
required.rationale: Writing $out.1 as ctl2-basics suggests fails at init.

required.check: status_cd is compared without trimming or nvl coercion, null-safely (`!=`/`==` are null-safe): null equals null, and an empty status differs from null (X → "" is a change; nvl(status, "") would hide null → "").
required.rationale: Coercing null to "" hides the null-to-empty change.

required.check: annual_value is compared as a typed decimal without nvl-to-zero or rounding: null differs from 0.00 and 2.00 → null is a change.
required.rationale: nvl(value, 0) equates null with zero.

required.check: expires_at is compared as the complete date value including time: 00:00:00 vs 00:00:01 on the same day is a change (no trunc/date2str to day), and null vs non-null differs.
required.rationale: Day-level comparison misses the one-second change.

required.check: cdc_action is UPDATE when any tracked field differs and UNCHANGED otherwise; customer_label, contract_note, timestamps and other ancillary fields are not compared.
required.rationale: Comparing ancillary fields turns unchanged pairs into updates.

required.check: changed_fields lists the differing field names in the order status_cd, annual_value, expires_at, joined by "," without spaces or trailing comma (`join(",", list)` or equivalent), and is the empty string (not null) for an unchanged pair.
required.rationale: Wrong order/separator or null for unchanged breaks the delta contract.

required.check: Two all-null tracked tuples are UNCHANGED (the first pair A with all-null fields).
required.rationale: A null-unsafe comparison marks the all-null pair as changed or throws.

required.check: All output snapshot fields come from the incoming record $in.1 (`$out.0.* = $in.1.*;` or per-field), keeping its nulls, blanks and zeros; only cdc_action and changed_fields are computed.
required.rationale: Copying $in.0 publishes the previous snapshot's values.

required.check: The change list/decision is reset for every pair (local declaration in transform() or explicit clearing each call), so each Cartesian pairing of duplicate keys gets its own result (E pairs: UNCHANGED, UPDATE, UPDATE, UNCHANGED).
required.rationale: A global list carries earlier differences into an unchanged pair.

forbidden.check: Writes one-sided records from transform() or fabricates removal/addition rows (e.g. INSERT/DELETE actions, writing `$out.2`).
forbidden.rationale: One-sided records are passed through by the component on ports 0 and 2; CTL sees only matched pairs.

forbidden.check: Returns SKIP (drops the pair) or STOP (the run ends in ERROR) for any matched pair, e.g. SKIP for unchanged pairs.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 5 requires unchanged pairs to be emitted; only OK/0/1/ALL emit.

T53.notes: Since `==`/`!=` are null-safe, the comparison itself is easy; items target null/empty coercion, full timestamps, $in.1 source and per-pair reset. The ctl2-basics §8.9 $out.1 statement contradicts the live run; item .1 states the verified fact.
